properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): the checksum-acceptance path defaulted a missing change_type to test_failure_fix, so every reconcile pass entered the fix population — 142 of reflow2's own 281 fix-typed events are acceptances, 104 wearing the default, none with a cause — and the gap's text then offered "this design does not record causes" as a live option, which an agent that had not read the rule took at face value
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL, the third walk of epoch:planned-the-mechanism-reaches-the-moment, on fact:a-work-project-answered-fix-without-recorded-cause-and-twenty-of-twenty-one-fixes-were-checksum-dispositions-wearing-the-nearest-label (relayed by Anthony, 2026-09-14).

① OBSERVED: the detector asked a project about 21 fixes with no cause; the agent answered that 20 were checksum dispositions recorded while reconciling the design with the code, "defect_fix was the closest label", and put to the owner whether the project should record causes at all — offering "C. Acknowledge it — [the project] doesn't record causes". Anthony: "the graph is recording information that the AI agent doesn't know what to do with"; "the agent shouldn't have to ask if it should record causes." Expected: a detector about repairs asks about repairs, and its text tells the reader what the rule is and how to triage, never whether to keep the rule. NOT affected: the three genuine repairs on that project had their causes recorded — the discipline works where the instruction reaches the moment of repairing.

② PRECEDENT, searched: fact:defect-the-checksum-disposition-has-no-answer-for-aligning-code-to-existing-intent (2026-08-14) already said the disposition vocabulary had no honest label for the commonest case and closed with "the confirmation ledger could count design_holds accepts carrying test_failure_fix — a sweep nobody has run". dec:the-no-cause-fix-gap-grandfathers-fixes-recorded-before-the-rule-existed (accepted 2026-09-07) rules a date boundary that the detector does not yet implement (it parks, it does not date). dec:change-type-splits-into-two-axes. The design's own doctrine on defaults, stated for `kind`, `priority` and `quality_target`: a default makes an unasked question indistinguishable from an answered one.

③ CANDIDATES from the bones: (a) CONTRACT — the tool's default labels a silent acceptance with a fix type. (b) ALLOCATION — the agent chose the nearest label by hand. (c) INTENT — the gap text phrases a DesignRule as a per-project choice. (d) ASSURANCE — the detector cannot tell an acceptance from a repair, so its population is wrong by construction. (e) NOT IN THE SUSPECTED COMPONENT — the 09-07 date-boundary ruling was never built, so old records keep arriving. (f) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG.

④/⑤ MEASURED 2026-09-14. (a) CONFIRMED at service.rs parse_disposition: `change_type.unwrap_or("test_failure_fix")` on design_holds; the schema advertised "(test_failure_fix default)". The sweep the 08-14 record asked for, run on reflow2's own export: 968 ChangeEvents, 281 fix-typed, 142 of them minted by acceptances (ids chg:accept-…): 104 test_failure_fix (the default) and 38 defect_fix; 0 of the 142 on any CAUSES edge. So the default alone puts half the fix population there; the field agent's "closest label" is (b), the same effect by hand. (c) CONFIRMED at detect.rs: the description ended "acknowledging this finding instead says this design does not record causes, and it will not be asked again" — the sentence the agent turned into option C; a grep of every served gap text found this the only one offering to decline a rule. (d) CONFIRMED: the detector read change_type alone; the acceptance marker (`accepted_baseline: true`) lives on the CHANGED edge the accept writes, so the two populations were separable and never separated. (e) CONFIRMED and out of scope: the detector has parking and no date boundary; recorded, not fixed here. (f) REFUTED.

⑥ THE CLASS: a typed constructor's DEFAULT silently answers a question nobody asked, and a detector downstream then asks a person to explain records nobody wrote. The design already names this class for three other fields and refuses to default them; this field was missed. Would the fix have stopped the 08-14 report? Partly: that report was about the missing label (as_built_aligned), which stays open; but the sweep it asked for is now run and the default it feared is gone. Would it have stopped THIS report? Yes on both halves: the twenty would have been asked for a reason at the moment of acceptance, and the one real question would have arrived with a recipe instead of an invitation to decline.

⑦ PINNED FIRST: crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/a_design_holds_acceptance_says_why_the_code_moved.rs — five tests, the two refusal cases observed failing (a baselined artifact accepted with no reason; the bulk form naming the silent item), the three permissive cases (a stated reason recorded as given; a repair may still say so; a first baseline needs no reason) passing before and after. crates/reflow2-core/tests/fix_without_recorded_cause.rs — three tests, two observed failing (an acceptance wearing a fix label is told apart from a repair and named for relabelling; the text states the discipline and a recipe and never offers to decline).

⑧ FIXED AT THE CAUSE, the three sub-items the field report recorded. (a) SOURCE: design_holds on an artifact that already has a baseline REQUIRES change_type; the refusal names the repair labels as repair-only and the reconcile labels (`resync`, `refactor`, `documentation`, `performance_optimization`); an artifact with no baseline is still read as a first baseline with nothing to ask; the bulk form refuses per item and names it. (b) TEXT: the gap is a standing rule with a triage recipe in order — your own fix: invalidates or record_finding with caused_by; an acceptance wearing a fix label: relabel, never invent a cause; a backlog predating the rule: park under one accepted Decision, forward-only; acknowledging records that the backlog was judged, not that the discipline was declined. (c) CONSTRUCTION: the detector tells acceptances (CHANGED edge marked accepted_baseline) from repairs; acceptances wearing a fix label are counted and named separately ("…, and N checksum acceptance(s) wear a fix label") and excluded from the repair denominator.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: on the field project, whether the agent or the default chose defect_fix (the agent said "closest label", which is (b); the default would have produced test_failure_fix); the as_built_aligned disposition stays an open idea; the date-boundary ruling of 09-07 is accepted and unbuilt; and reflow2's own 142 mislabelled acceptances are now NAMED by the detector, not relabelled — that is a triage pass for a session with the owner's word, per the recipe.
